summary: Eight comment-endorsed discoveries spanning agent workflows, personal apps, and hardware; 90-day history cooldown applied.
telegram_footer: 8 items surfaced | 30/30 stories fully crawled · 5,814 comments | history + run artifact updated

items.name: Remuda
items.source_story_title: Ask HN: What's your current AI agentic setup?
items.summary: A CLI for launching coding agents; its creator praises a lightweight, hackable workflow.
items.why_included: A concrete agent launcher backed by an explicitly positive account of sustained use from its creator.
items.evidence: The creator describes the workflow as light and hackable, says it works well, and has felt little need to switch.

evidence_sources.author: dgunay
evidence_sources.excerpt: It's not nearly as polished as some of the software factory setups and fancy GUI orchestrators I'm seeing, but it's light, hackable, and so far the bitter lesson has kept this working really well for me so I haven't felt much of a need to try anything else.

items.name: Editor Code Assistant
items.source_story_title: Ask HN: What's your current AI agentic setup?
items.summary: An editor-agnostic AI coding assistant; an Emacs user calls it their go-to harness.
items.why_included: A clear first-hand preference for an editor-native harness rather than a bare project mention.
items.evidence: An Emacs user prefers Editor Code Assistant as their go-to harness; connecting OpenCode required some fiddling but now works.

evidence_sources.author: eamonnsullivan
evidence_sources.excerpt: I mostly use Editor Code Assistant [2] with Emacs as my go-to harness. I've set up ECA to use OpenCode as a provider, which was a little fiddly compared with more mainstream options, but it's working now.

items.name: ctlflow
items.source_story_title: Ask HN: What's your current AI agentic setup?
items.summary: A Matrix-connected agent fleet system; a user praises its large-data research capabilities.
items.why_included: A first-hand account identifies useful non-coding research work rather than merely advertising an agent framework.
items.evidence: A user reports running dozens of agents for tasks such as equity analysis and finding the information surfaced from large datasets surprising.

evidence_sources.author: jeswin
evidence_sources.excerpt: For non coding usecases, I use https://www.ctlflow.com. This lets me run dozens of agents on tasks like equity analysis. The information a swarm of agents can surface from a large data store can be quite surprising.

items.name: SUB/WAVE
items.source_story_title: I wish tech companies knew more about me
items.summary: A self-hosted radio station with an AI DJ, playing your own music collection.
items.why_included: An enthusiastic first-hand endorsement offers a concrete alternative to opaque streaming recommendations.
items.evidence: A user calls SUB/WAVE great but notes that recommendations are limited to their existing music collection and wishes for streaming-service integration.

evidence_sources.author: pbnjay
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've been using https://www.getsubwave.com lately and it's great, but it is unfortunately already pre-filtered to my music collection. Would be slick to connect to spotify or a streaming service though!

items.name: Ecosia
items.summary: A European search engine; a former Kagi user reports a satisfying switch.
items.why_included: A direct comparison grounded in personal use makes this search alternative more than a topical mention.
items.evidence: A former Kagi user says Ecosia has not been frustrating and cannot call it worse than Kagi, while wishing for a paid option instead of ads.

evidence_sources.author: palata
evidence_sources.excerpt: Ecosia hasn't been frustrating though, and I cannot say that it's worse than my experience with Kagi. I just wish I could pay Ecosia instead of having ads (which my browser seems to block anyway).

items.name: Window Sweaters
items.summary: A macOS menu-bar app that adds knitted window borders; charming, but still unpolished.
items.why_included: Independent comment praise and creator-reported daily use support a playful desktop discovery, with its rough edges made explicit.
items.evidence: One commenter explicitly loves the window sweaters; the creator says they use the app every day but acknowledges it is not polished.

evidence_sources.author: nico
evidence_sources.excerpt: So cool, thank you for the context. And love the window sweaters!

evidence_sources.author: gordic_sara
evidence_sources.excerpt: It’s not a polished product, but I use it every day and I’m still fixing things when I can.

items.name: Moto G Power
items.summary: A budget Android phone praised for durability and battery life, not compactness.
items.why_included: A strong ownership-based endorsement of an affordable phone surfaced inside a flagship discussion.
items.evidence: An owner calls Moto G Power their favorite phone, praises its price, durability and battery life, and says their 2024 model is still going strong; they wish it were smaller.

evidence_sources.author: unregistereddev
evidence_sources.excerpt: Moto G Power is my favorite phone. Cheap enough I don't bother with a case. Durable enough that I haven't regretted not buying a case. The extra battery life allows me to keep using the phone long after the battery starts to degrade. I've run a g power for 4 years straight, only replacing it because the phone had become unusably slow. My current 2024 model is still going strong and I have no plans to replace it. But man I wish it were smaller.

items.name: Omarchy
items.summary: A Linux desktop distribution praised on a MacBook; M-series installation support remains disputed.
items.why_included: A positive daily-driver report warrants resurfacing after the cooldown, but conflicting support information prevents an unqualified Mac recommendation.
items.evidence: A MacBook user says Omarchy works great and reports working TouchID and speakers; a reply quotes documentation saying M-series installation is not directly supported.

evidence_sources.author: gorilla_fight
evidence_sources.excerpt: TouchID is already supported on Omarchy, I use it on my daily driver MacBook works great. The speaker too.

evidence_sources.author: justauserid
evidence_sources.excerpt: Please note that installing on an M-series Mac is not directly supported at this time.
